issues.legal_issue: A claimant relying on co-sharer status must establish that the status continued in the land subject to pre-emption through the date of decree.
material_facts: The claimants brought a pre-emption suit on the basis that they were co-sharers in the lands sold.
Before the trial court decreed the suit, the claimants transferred their co-ownership rights in most of the relevant holdings and asserted that they retained a smaller area.
They did not establish that the area said to have been retained was in the holdings containing the land subject to pre-emption.
issues.conclusion: The claimants had not established co-sharer status in the land subject to pre-emption on the date of decree and were not entitled to a pre-emption decree; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 15(b) fourthly of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, a claimant relying on co-sharer status must establish the relevant status both when the sale becomes effective and through the date of decree. Section 3(3)'s definition of a holding does not make every owner of land in an estate a co-sharer in every parcel in that estate. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: preemption_suit and claimant_relies_on_coshare_status and claimant_transferred_coshare_rights_before_decree and retained_share_in_suit_land_unproved

predicates.preemption_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking to pre-empt a sale of land.
predicates.claimant_relies_on_coshare_status: The claimant based the claimed right to pre-empt on being a co-sharer in the land sold.
predicates.claimant_transferred_coshare_rights_befo: The claimant transferred co-ownership rights in the relevant holdings before the decree was made.
predicates.retained_share_in_suit_land_unproved: The claimant did not prove that any retained share was in the holdings containing the land subject to pre-emption.
predicates.claimant_not_entitled_to_preemption: The claimant is not entitled to obtain a decree for pre-emption.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a pre-emption suit relies on co-sharer status, transfers co-ownership rights before decree, and fails to prove a retained share in the land subject to pre-emption, the claimant is not entitled to pre-emption.

issues.legal_issue: A court may draw an adverse inference when a claimant fails to produce a material document in the claimant's possession that could establish the claimed continuing co-ownership.
material_facts: The claimants asserted that they had retained a small area in the relevant holdings after transferring their other co-ownership rights.
The sale deed recording the transfer was not produced, although it was in the claimants' power and possession and could have shown whether any relevant land had been retained.
The claimants did not establish by other evidence that the retained area was in the holdings containing the land subject to pre-emption.
issues.conclusion: The omission justified an adverse inference that the sale deed would have shown that the claimants retained no land relevant to their pre-emption claim; oral evidence did not cure the failure to establish the claimed interest.
issues.legal_principle: A court may draw an adverse inference from a party's failure to produce a material document within that party's power and possession. The judgment applies this principle to the claimants' failure to produce the transfer deed; it cites no earlier cases for the principle.

rule.if: preemption_suit and material_transfer_document_in_claimant_control and claimant_failed_to_produce_document and document_could_show_retained_interest

predicates.preemption_suit: The claimant brought a suit seeking to pre-empt a sale of land.
predicates.material_transfer_document_in_claimant_c: A document recording the claimant's transfer of co-ownership rights was within the claimant's power and possession.
predicates.claimant_failed_to_produce_document: The claimant did not produce that transfer document.
predicates.document_could_show_retained_interest: The transfer document could establish whether the claimant retained an interest in the land subject to pre-emption.
predicates.adverse_inference_against_claimant_justi: The court is justified in inferring that the withheld document would not support the claimant's assertion of a retained interest.

issues.definition: When a claimant in a pre-emption suit withholds a transfer document in the claimant's control that could establish a retained interest, an adverse inference against the claimant is justified.
